content.text: {"screening_id":"SCR_000083","question_assessments":[{"domain_id":"D1","question_id":"1.1","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Page 2, Methods—Randomization","evidence_summary":"Participants were randomized 1:1 using computer-generated block sizes of 4, 6, and 8, stratified by sex, type 2 diabetes, and study site.","rationale":"A computer-generated sequence with randomly varying block sizes is an appropriate random allocation method.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D1","question_id":"1.2","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Page 2, Methods—Randomization","evidence_summary":"Randomization was implemented through Castor Electronic Data Capture. Allocation results were visible only to trial pharmacists who prepared medication and were otherwise uninvolved in the study.","rationale":"Central electronic assignment with access restricted to uninvolved pharmacists supports concealment until enrollment and assignment.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D1","question_id":"1.3","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Pages 4-5, Results—Patients; Table 1","evidence_summary":"Demographic, clinical, medication, kidney-function, and surgical characteristics were generally similar between the two randomized groups.","rationale":"The small observed differences are compatible with chance and do not suggest failure of randomization.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.1","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Pages 2-3, Methods—Randomization and Intervention","evidence_summary":"The trial was double-blind, and dapagliflozin and placebo were supplied as matching capsules.","rationale":"Matching medication and double-blind administration make participant awareness of assignment unlikely.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.2","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Pages 2-3, Methods—Randomization and Intervention","evidence_summary":"Allocation was known only to trial pharmacists who prepared medication and were otherwise uninvolved; hospital staff and study personnel administered matching capsules.","rationale":"Carers and intervention providers were adequately blinded to assignment.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.3","agent_response":"PN","evidence_location":"Page 4, Figure 1; Results—Patients","evidence_summary":"Not all participants received all four doses: 344 of 392 in the dapagliflozin group and 339 of 392 in the placebo group took all doses. Reasons for missed doses were not reported.","rationale":"Some nonadherence occurred, but there is no indication that it resulted from the experimental context, and blinding reduces the likelihood of assignment-related deviations.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.4","agent_response":"PN","evidence_location":"Pages 4 and 6-7, Figure 1; Results—Exploratory Outcomes","evidence_summary":"Full adherence was high and similar between groups. The per-protocol result was also similar to the primary result: AKI occurred in 27% versus 51%, relative risk 0.52.","rationale":"Given the limited, balanced nonadherence and robustness of the result in adherent participants, deviations were unlikely to materially affect the target result.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.5","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Page 4, Figure 1; Results—Patients","evidence_summary":"Eighty-eight percent of dapagliflozin participants and 87% of placebo participants took all four doses; 4 versus 1 participants took no doses.","rationale":"The frequency of incomplete treatment was closely balanced between randomized groups.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.6","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Page 4, Figure 1; Pages 5-6, Results—Primary Outcome and Table 2","evidence_summary":"All 392 participants randomized to each group were included in the primary analysis, with results reported according to randomized assignment.","rationale":"This intention-to-treat approach is appropriate for estimating the effect of assignment to dapagliflozin versus placebo.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D2","question_id":"2.7","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Page 4, Figure 1; Pages 5-6, Table 2","evidence_summary":"The primary analysis retained all randomized participants in their assigned groups.","rationale":"There was no failure to analyze participants according to randomized assignment, so this question does not apply.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D3","question_id":"3.1","agent_response":"Y","evidence_location":"Page 1, Abstract—Results; Page 4, Figure 1; Pages 5-6, Table 2","evidence_summary":"Follow-up testing was completed by 778 of 784 participants (99%), and the primary analysis reported all 392 randomized participants in each group.","rationale":"Outcome data were available for all or nearly all randomized participants; any unavailable postoperative observations involved less than 1% of the randomized sample.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D3","question_id":"3.2","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Page 1, Abstract—Results; Page 4, Figure 1","evidence_summary":"Follow-up was 99%, and all randomized participants were represented in the primary analysis denominators.","rationale":"Because outcome data were available for nearly all participants, additional evidence demonstrating absence of bias from missing data is not required.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D3","question_id":"3.3","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Page 1, Abstract—Results; Page 4, Figure 1","evidence_summary":"Only six participants did not complete follow-up testing, while all randomized participants appeared in the primary analysis.","rationale":"With negligible missing outcome data, dependence of missingness on the true AKI outcome is not a material concern for this result.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D3","question_id":"3.4","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Page 1, Abstract—Results; Page 4, Figure 1","evidence_summary":"The extent of potentially missing outcome information was less than 1%.","rationale":"The question is not applicable after determining that data were available for nearly all randomized participants.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.1","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Page 3, Methods—Primary Outcomes","evidence_summary":"AKI was defined using KDIGO criteria based on prespecified changes in serum creatinine or reduced urine output. Creatinine was measured daily for up to seven postoperative days while hospitalized, and urine output was recorded hourly while a catheter was present.","rationale":"KDIGO creatinine and urine-output criteria are established and appropriate methods for measuring postoperative AKI.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.2","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Pages 2-3, Methods—Intervention and Primary Outcomes","evidence_summary":"The same creatinine and urine-output criteria and measurement schedule applied to both groups, and clinical and study personnel were blinded.","rationale":"There is no evidence that measurement or ascertainment procedures differed by randomized group.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.3","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Pages 2-3, Methods—Randomization, Intervention, and Primary Outcomes","evidence_summary":"The study was double-blind; only medication-preparing pharmacists knew allocation and they were otherwise not involved in the study.","rationale":"Personnel measuring or recording creatinine and urine output were unlikely to know intervention assignment.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.4","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Pages 2-3, Methods—Randomization and Primary Outcomes","evidence_summary":"Outcome assessors were blinded, and the outcome was based on quantitative laboratory and urine-output thresholds.","rationale":"Because assessors were unaware of allocation, the possibility that knowledge could influence assessment is not applicable.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D4","question_id":"4.5","agent_response":"NA","evidence_location":"Pages 2-3, Methods—Randomization and Primary Outcomes","evidence_summary":"AKI ascertainment used objective thresholds under blinded conditions.","rationale":"There was no assessor knowledge of intervention assignment that could have influenced outcome assessment.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D5","question_id":"5.1","agent_response":"PY","evidence_location":"Pages 2-4, Methods—Trial Design, Primary Outcomes, Statistical Analysis, and Sample Size Calculation; Page 8, Limitations; trial registration NCT05590143","evidence_summary":"The trial was registered, the protocol was reported as previously published and available in Supplement 1, and the primary AKI outcome and analysis methods were described as prespecified. The paper notes that adjustment for all stratification factors was post hoc.","rationale":"The unadjusted randomized-group comparison corresponds to the stated primary outcome and planned methods. Although the supplied article does not establish every protocol timestamp directly, it probably followed a plan finalized before unblinded outcome data were available.","agent_confidence":"Moderate"},{"domain_id":"D5","question_id":"5.2","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Pages 1 and 3, Abstract—Main Outcome and Methods—Primary Outcomes; Pages 5-6, Table 2","evidence_summary":"The reported result uses the stated seven-day KDIGO composite outcome, incorporating prespecified creatinine and urine-output criteria. Separate component analyses were explicitly labeled post hoc.","rationale":"The primary numerical result matches the prespecified outcome definition and does not appear selected from multiple eligible outcome measurements.","agent_confidence":"High"},{"domain_id":"D5","question_id":"5.3","agent_response":"N","evidence_location":"Pages 3-4, Methods—Statistical Analysis; Pages 5-7, Table 2 and Results—Primary, Exploratory, and Post Hoc Outcomes","evidence_summary":"The primary result was the unadjusted randomized-group comparison. Sex-adjusted, per-protocol, and stratification-factor-adjusted analyses were separately identified as secondary, exploratory, or post hoc and gave similar findings.","rationale":"Although several supportive analyses were performed, the reported primary estimate corresponds to the stated primary analysis and does not appear chosen based on statistical significance or effect size.","agent_confidence":"High"}],"domain_assessments":[{"domain_id":"D1","provisional_domain_judgement":"Low","domain_rationale":"The allocation sequence was computer-generated, assignment was concealed through a central electronic system with restricted pharmacist access, and baseline characteristics showed no concerning imbalance."},{"domain_id":"D2","provisional_domain_judgement":"Low","domain_rationale":"Participants and providers were blinded, incomplete adherence was limited and balanced, and the primary analysis included all participants according to randomized assignment. The per-protocol analysis supported the same conclusion."},{"domain_id":"D3","provisional_domain_judgement":"Low","domain_rationale":"Follow-up was completed for 99% of randomized participants, and all randomized participants were represented in the primary analysis denominators; missing outcome data were therefore unlikely to bias the result."},{"domain_id":"D4","provisional_domain_judgement":"Low","domain_rationale":"Postoperative AKI was measured in both groups using the same established KDIGO creatinine and urine-output thresholds under blinded conditions."},{"domain_id":"D5","provisional_domain_judgement":"Low","domain_rationale":"The reported result corresponds to the stated prespecified seven-day primary outcome and primary randomized-group analysis. Alternative and post hoc analyses were clearly distinguished and produced consistent results."}],"agent_overall_provisional_judgement":"Low","agent_overall_rationale":"The target result arose from a well-concealed, double-blind randomized trial with balanced baseline characteristics, near-complete outcome data, objective and consistently applied AKI criteria, intention-to-treat analysis, and no evident selective reporting. Minor uncertainty about the timing and complete details of the prespecified analysis plan does not warrant raising the overall judgement."}
